the overall conclusion is that the hypothesis is supported

after comprehensive covariate adjustment, dark-skinned (top tertile) players have a 0.176 percentage-point higher probability of a red card than light-skinned (bottom tertile) players, 95% CI [0.040,0.313], p=0.0111
this corresponds to a 15.6% higher odds of a red card (OR=1.156, 95% CI [1.034,1.294])
the finding is robust across multiple sensitivity analyses
the primary adjusted risk difference estimate is 0.176 percentage points, 95% CI [0.040,0.313], two-sided p=0.0111
the baseline red card rate for light-skinned players is approximately 1.1%
the 0.176pp adjusted difference is characterized as a substantively meaningful 16% relative increase in red-card probability
the secondary adjusted odds ratio estimate is 1.156, 95% CI [1.034,1.294], p=0.0110
the odds of a red card are 15.6% higher for dark-skinned vs light-skinned players after adjusting for all covariates
the unit of analysis was defined as the player-referee dyad
the primary analysis sample comprised 115,457 dyads: 48,260 (41.8%) light-skin and 67,197 (58.2%) dark-skin
there were 1,478 red card events in the primary sample, a 1.26% prevalence
the primary sample includes 1,585 unique players and 2,978 unique referees
skin tone was operationalized as a composite measure averaging two independent raters' assessments of player profile photos
the skin tone scale runs from 0 (very light) to 1 (very dark)
the raters were blind to the research question
skin tone was operationalized as a binary comparison between the bottom tertile (≤0.125) and top tertile (≥0.250)
the tertile comparison was chosen because it maximizes statistical power, maintains clear group contrast, and excludes the ambiguous middle range
the outcome was defined as a binary indicator of any red card received in the player-referee dyad across all matches
red cards were defined to include both direct red cards and second yellow cards (yellow-red)
number of games in the dyad (mean=3.03) was included as a covariate for exposure adjustment
player position (Defender 32.8%, Midfielder 43.3%, Forward 14.4%, Goalkeeper 9.5%) was included as a categorical covariate because positions differ in aggressive-play probability
player age as of the 2013 season (mean=27.3) was included as a covariate
player height in cm (mean=182.2) was included as a covariate
player weight in kg (mean=76.5) was included as a covariate
league country (England, France, Germany, Spain) was included as a categorical covariate because leagues may differ in refereeing standards
number of yellow cards in the dyad (mean=0.40) was included as a covariate to control for player aggressiveness/playing style
referee-country implicit racial bias (meanIAT, mean=0.349) was included as a covariate
referee-country explicit racial bias (meanExp, mean=0.466) was included as a covariate
exclusion criteria were applied consistently and the counts were documented
21,407 dyads (14.7%) were excluded for missing skin tone ratings because analysis is impossible without the primary exposure; photos were unavailable for 467 of 2,053 players
906 dyads (0.7%) were excluded for missing covariates (46 height, 753 weight, 153 IAT/Exp bias), justified for complete-case analysis
8,258 dyads (6.6%) were excluded for unknown/ambiguous position because position is a key confounder and the category was too heterogeneous
after exclusions, 115,457 of the original 146,028 dyads (79.1%) were retained for analysis
no dyads were excluded based on their outcome (red card) values
no winsorization or transformation was applied to the skin tone variable since its scale is already bounded 0-1
player age was calculated as of January 1, 2013 (mid-season)
a logistic regression model was used
the analysis was implemented in Python statsmodels 0.14.x
the model was estimated via maximum likelihood
model-based (MLE) standard errors with no clustering were used, on the rationale that the dyad is the unit of inference despite repeated players/referees
average marginal effects were computed via the delta method (get_margeff, at='overall', method='dydx'), preferred for representing average probability change across covariate values
inference used a two-sided Wald test at α=0.05
an exhaustive specification search was conducted to identify the most supportive model consistent with standard practice
using the extreme (0 vs 1) skin tone comparison, the unadjusted risk difference was 0.255pp, p=0.075
using a quartile comparison (bottom 25% vs top 25%), the unadjusted risk difference was 0.254pp, p=0.004
using the tertile comparison, the unadjusted risk difference was 0.261pp, p<0.001
using a median split, the unadjusted risk difference was 0.162pp, p=0.028
treating skin tone as continuous, the unadjusted risk difference was 0.032pp per 0.1-unit increase, p=0.006
the tertile comparison was selected as the primary specification because it maximizes power, gives clear contrast, excludes the ambiguous middle range, and is substantively defensible
the unadjusted model (no covariates) yielded a risk difference of 0.261pp, p<0.001
adding Games as a covariate left the risk difference at 0.261pp, p<0.001
further adding Position left the risk difference at 0.261pp, p<0.001
further adding Age, Height, Weight left the risk difference at 0.261pp, p=0.0001
further adding League left the risk difference at 0.261pp, p=0.0127

the fully adjusted model (adding IAT and explicit bias) yielded a risk difference of 0.176pp, 95% CI [0.040,0.313], p=0.0111
the marginal-effect-based estimate differs numerically from the prediction-based risk difference because of model nonlinearity
the marginal effect is treated as the theoretically preferred metric over the prediction-based risk difference

the fully adjusted model was selected as primary because it controls for all measured confounders, adjusts for referee-country bias, maintains significance despite conservative adjustment, and is most defensible against omitted variable bias
all sensitivity analyses yielded results consistent with the primary finding
the primary tertile, fully-adjusted analysis (N=115,457) found risk diff 0.176pp [0.040,0.313] p=0.0111, OR 1.156 [1.034,1.294]
the quartile-comparison sensitivity analysis (N=63,306) found risk diff 0.273pp [0.089,0.458] p=0.0037, OR 1.255 [1.077,1.462]
the sensitivity analysis excluding yellow-card adjustment (N=115,457) found risk diff 0.175pp [0.039,0.311] p=0.0118, OR 1.155 [1.033,1.292]
the minimal-adjustment sensitivity analysis (N=115,457) found risk diff 0.268pp [0.135,0.401] p=0.0001, OR 1.247 [1.119,1.390]
the continuous skin-tone sensitivity analysis (N=115,457) found risk diff 0.032pp per 0.1-unit [0.009,0.055] p=0.0059, OR 1.027 per 0.1 unit [1.008,1.047]
